newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds claw back earlier losses.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds claw back earlier losses.

text.p: 1550 GMT - Austrian bonds recovered from early morning losses to stand marginally firm in late afternoon after choppy trade.
"In the morning there was some pretty hefty profittaking," said one trader. "Later on some money then came back into the market."
Traders see Bund trading between 100.50 and 101.00 points.
* Latest 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 down 20 bps at 99.45 to yield 5.95 (5.92) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 99.43/53 to yield 5.95/93.
* At the near end, five-year 5.50 percent bond maturing March 2001 down 20 bps at 102.65 to yield 4.84 (4.79) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 102.72/82 to yield 4.82/80 percent.
* 10-year spread to German bunds steady at 11 bps, five-year spread down four at 16 bps.
* December AGB future up 21 bps at 106.99 on volume of 150 contracts.
* Money market rates mixed with three-month VIBOR higher at 3.330 and overnight money steady at 3.04/29. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
